summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 89% to ₹186.21 crores, with EBITDA of ₹101.71 crores (55% margin) and PAT of ₹84.27 crores.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was ₹186.21 crores, up 89% YoY, with EBITDA of ₹101.71 crores (55% margin, up 155%) and PAT of ₹84.27 crores (45% margin, up 267%). The company secured a ₹256.92 crore New Mangalore maintenance dredging contract (15.9 million cubic metres over 3 annual cycles) and acquired the TSHD River Pearl 48. Charter and hire added a third Green Tug contract (Mumbai Port, ₹236 crores, 15 years), and shipbuilding won a ₹62 crore IWAI order for 10 hybrid ferries. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to about 80% from 60%, and said EBITDA margin should stay above 45%.

financial_highlights.value: ~₹1,732.55 crores (dredging ₹467.75 crores, charter and hire ₹1,100 crores, shipbuilding ₹164 crores, excluding ₹275 crores captive shipbuilding)

financial_highlights.change: Management says Q2 was 3x Q2 last year

segments.name: Dredging
segments.commentary: Won the ₹256.92 crore New Mangalore maintenance dredging contract (15.9 million cubic metres over 3 cycles) and acquired River Pearl 48 TSHD, with management citing roughly 8-10 million cubic metres per annum and revenue above ₹150 crores per annum from that vessel. Dredging order book is ₹467.75 crores.

segments.name: Charter and Hire
segments.commentary: Third Green Tug contract from Mumbai Port (₹236 crores, 15 years), taking three Green Tug contracts to about ₹928 crores aggregate. Charter order book is ₹1,100 crores; management says vessels deployed on long-term contracts run at 100% utilisation.

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Won a ₹62 crore IWAI order for 10 electric hybrid passenger ferries. Shipbuilding order book is ₹164 crores excluding ₹275 crores of captive orders. Saphale yard Phase 1 targeted for February 2027, with full commissioning after Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to about 80% (from 60%, earlier 30-40%); management cited current and expected order inflows.
FY27 effective tax rate about 15%; FY28 and FY29 expected near 15% or below, with 25% corporate tax on shipbuilding profit.
Shipbuilding expected to be about 40% of overall revenue in FY28 and FY29, with dredging and chartering the remaining 60%.
Shipbuilding revenue expected to grow 3x-4x in FY27 versus FY26.
EBITDA margin expected to stay above 45% going forward, with the 50-55% H1 level seen as current expansion; prior guidance was 35-40%.
Order book expected to stay above ₹2,000 crores on a continual basis from next year; pipeline of bids ₹2,500-3,000 crores. Pipeline above ₹3,500 crores was cited earlier in the call.
capex_capacity: River Pearl 48 TSHD acquired, roughly a fourfold increase in hopper capacity; the second dredger is tied up awaiting a contract before capex.
Saphale shipyard Phase 1 targeted for February 2027; full commissioning after Q4 FY27, with vessel construction in parallel.
₹1,000 crore capex plan over 2 years, about 6-7 months in; funds used for the TSHD, 3 green tugs, 1 conventional tug and other plants. Expected asset turnover of 1:1 to 1:1.5.
Vessels deployed in India: 21 dredgers plus about 30 chartering vessels. Dredging vessels in NW-1 and NW-16 at 100% utilisation from October.
demand_pricing: Maintenance dredging segment is about 150 million cubic metres per annum across major and minor ports; the company's vessel can handle 8-10 million cubic metres per annum.
Indian maintenance dredging is about ₹2,000 crores annually, with capital dredging averaging about ₹3,000 crores per year. NW-1 and NW-16 contribute about ₹2,000 crores annually.
Government Green Tug programme needs about 98 green tugs across major ports; about 1,000 craft to be converted to green before 2047.
Shipbuilding is in talks with 3 clients on export orders, pending commercial negotiations.
Competition exists in all three segments; management cites execution edge and USPs to maintain margins. No pricing commentary given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% for the full year. Q2 rate was 23% due to interest income and shipbuilding profit. Going forward, the rate depends on the shipbuilding mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market size from large-scale dredging?
qa_highlights.answer: The vessel can dredge 8-10 million cubic metres per annum, with revenue above ₹150 crores per annum. Per-cubic-metre rates vary by port.

qa_highlights.question: How will River Pearl 48 be kept utilised after New Mangalore?
qa_highlights.answer: Bids are placed for other major ports and West Coast defence and naval projects, with outcomes expected in the current month. Moves between projects take under 15 days a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a delay risk to FY28-29 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no substantial delay risk. Dredging vessels are pre-positioned, New Mangalore work starts before 15 November, and no shipbuilding contracts face delay penalties.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Above 45% going forward once stable, with current expansion possibly reaching 50-55%. Previous guidance was 35-40%.

qa_highlights.question: How is shipbuilding billed and what is the working capital impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Payments are staged over 5-10 milestones certified by class or flag. Up to 10% of contract value can be drawn upfront against bank guarantees or surety bonds, so working capital need is limited.

risks_watch: Revenue is concentrated in dredging and charter contracts, and Q2 is seasonally soft due to monsoons. Q3 and Q4 are expected to show a sharp revenue jump.
Revenue from Bahrain is paused for safety and insurance reasons; Myanmar revenue is nil and no vessels are being moved there. Current-year revenue from both is almost nil.
Growth depends on winning new bids: the River Pearl 48 redeployment and other large tenders need outcomes soon. Pipeline is ₹2,500-3,000 crores in bids.
Saphale yard commissioning slips to after Q4 FY27 with Phase 1 targeted for February 2027. Delay could affect shipbuilding ramp-up and the 3-4x FY27 growth target.
Management said debt will be raised as needed alongside internal accruals to fund the ₹1,000 crore capex; leverage was not quantified.
Margin sustainability: H1 EBITDA margin of 55% is well above the earlier 35-40% range, and management did not give a detailed breakdown.
Unallocable expenses of about ₹10 crores in segment results were explained as corporate costs that cannot be assigned to either segment.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, guidance and margins, with specific numbers on contracts and capacity. Less specific on bid outcomes, the second dredger and export orders, which were described only as pending or in discussion.
key_quotes: Our objective is not simply to grow larger, but to build a stronger and more sustainable organization capable of delivering consistent long-term value.
All our projects are time-based and time sensitive.
The New Mangalore maintenance dredging contract represents a significant leap in our scale and responsibility.
